verses.verse:
मध्यमांश्च समुत्थाप्य नादः षष्ठ उदीयते।
समुत्थाप्य ततः सर्वान् प्रथमा नामिकाम् विना।८५।
verses.text: By lifting the middle fingers the sixth sound arises. Then, by lifting all of them except the first ring finger,

verses.verse:
प्राणाधातस्य वेगेन नाद्यते सप्तमः स्वरः।
ततः सर्वान् समाच्छाद्य तार निनाद्यते।८६।
verses.text: with the force of the stroke of breath the seventh note is sounded. Then, covering all [the holes], the tāra (upper) [Sa] is sounded.

commentary.text: In the same order, lifting the next finger, that is, the middle finger, produces the sixth sound, that is, dhaivata (Dha), and lifting the last, the index finger, produces the seventh sound, called niṣāda (Ni). But the force of the breath, rising step by step, becomes so great by Ni that if, blowing with that same force, we close all the holes at once, the eighth sound, that is, Ṡa of the tāra (upper) octave, is produced.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
